title: Leap Year
statement:
Decide whether a year is a leap year.

A year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4 but not by 100. Years divisible by 400 are the exception: they are always leap years. So 2024 and 2000 are leap years, while 2023 and 1900 are not.

The input is one positive integer `year` on a single line. Print `true` when it is a leap year and `false` otherwise.

Input:

```text
2024
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```
hints: Use the remainder operator `%` to test whether one number divides another.
Check your rule against 1900 and 2000. Both are divisible by 100, but only one of them is a leap year.

python.solution:
def is_leap_year(year: int) -> bool:
    return (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or year % 400 == 0


year = int(input())
print("true" if is_leap_year(year) else "false")
